policy_title: Digital Literacy Target and Clear Terms and Conditions
stated: Set a UK-wide target for digital literacy and require all products to provide short, clear terms and conditions outlining key facts on data and privacy, empowering consumers.

source.quote: Empower consumers and ensure that everyone can enjoy the benefits of new technology, by setting a UK-wide target for digital literacy and requiring all products to provide a short, clear version of their terms and conditions, setting out the key facts as they relate to individuals’ data and privacy.

bearing_set.reason: A UK-wide digital literacy target is explicitly a skills policy, bearing directly on adults' ability to acquire relevant skills and children's educational attainment in a digital economy — within O7's scope of FE/skills and attainment.
Mandatory short, clear T&Cs on data and privacy directly concerns consumers' ability to understand and exercise their privacy rights — privacy is explicitly within O9's strict scope.
Mandating short, clear T&Cs outlining data and privacy practices directly empowers consumers' effective privacy autonomy — bearing on the 'privacy / surveillance' indicator of personal liberty.

membership_note: The two components map cleanly to two distinct fundamentals: the literacy target to O7 (skills/education) and the T&Cs requirement to O10 (privacy autonomy). Effects on O13 (prosperity via digital skills) and O14 (narrowing digital exclusion gaps) are plausible but downstream and insufficiently specific to the policy's mechanism to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
